s1.syndrome_frame: Painless scrotal swelling with testicular enlargement and solid masses
salient_findings: Large, solid masses in both testes
Pleomorphic tumor with three distinct cell types
key_facts: 63-year-old man
8-month history of painless scrotal swelling
Bilateral testicular enlargement without tenderness
Scrotal ultrasound showed large, solid masses in both testes
Serum β-human chorionic gonadotropin, α-fetoprotein, and lactate dehydrogenase were within normal limits
No evidence of lymphadenopathy or extranodal lymphomatous masses on PET-CT scan
Left radical inguinal orchiectomy was performed
Tumor confined to the testis with lymphovascular invasion
Histologic examination demonstrated a pleomorphic tumor composed of small, medium, and large cells

shortlist.label: Mixed germ cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Pleomorphic tumor with multiple cell types and lymphovascular invasion

shortlist.label: Embryonal carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Painless scrotal swelling and solid masses in both testes, with tumor confined to the testis

shortlist.label: Seminoma
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral testicular enlargement without tenderness and normal serum tumor markers

shortlist.label: Teratoma
shortlist.why_kept: Pleomorphic tumor with multiple cell types and solid masses in both testes

shortlist.label: Germ cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Testicular enlargement and solid masses, with lymphovascular invasion and normal serum tumor markers

raw.rationale: The histologic examination demonstrated a pleomorphic tumor composed of three distinct cell types, which is consistent with a mixed germ cell tumor, and the presence of lymphovascular invasion and normal tumor markers also support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Embryonal carcinoma
rejected.why: Embryonal carcinoma typically presents with elevated α-fetoprotein levels, which were within normal limits in this case

rejected.label: Seminoma
rejected.why: Seminoma is typically composed of uniform cells and often presents with elevated β-human chorionic gonadotropin levels, which were within normal limits in this case

rejected.label: Teratoma
rejected.why: Teratoma is a type of germ cell tumor that typically contains several different types of tissues, but the histologic examination in this case described a pleomorphic tumor composed of small, medium, and large cells, which is more consistent with a mixed germ cell tumor

rejected.label: Germ cell tumor
rejected.why: Germ cell tumor is a broad category that includes several different types of tumors, including mixed germ cell tumor, but the specific characteristics of the tumor in this case make mixed germ cell tumor a more specific and accurate diagnosis
